Welcome

“This is a prototype: you’re helping shape it.”

We could stop the bully, if we all stood up together.

We didn’t.

“Stand up on your own and you just get pushed to the ground.”
ChatIn the chat

One word for your own playground moment.

Read out two or three words.

In every battle, each of us is safer running.

“The guards are running. Horatius shames a couple of them into standing with him.”

Mosul, 2014: a few thousand fighters took a city from an army many times their size.

Each soldier saw others leaving, and went too.

“Once the line starts to go, nobody wants to be the last one standing.”

Authoritarian regimes last for decades, then fall almost overnight.

“Why did so few stand up to the Nazis, or to Stalin?”

First they came for the socialists, and I did not speak out, because I was not a socialist.

Then they came for the trade unionists, and I did not speak out, because I was not a trade unionist.

Then they came for the Jews, and I did not speak out, because I was not a Jew.

Then they came for me, and there was no one left to speak for me.

Martin Niemöller
“We didn’t stand up for the others.”

When everyone sees everyone else in the streets, it’s suddenly safe to go.

Potsdamer Platz, 14 November 1989 · US Department of Defense · public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

“A sudden coordination moment. Same people, same regime, and overnight it’s over.”

We’d all be better off with a shared commons.

Each of us does better keeping ours closed.

“Open source, open data, open knowledge. Mostly, we didn’t.”

The biggest commons of all is the planet.

We’d all be better off cutting emissions.

None of us can afford to go first alone.

“That’s environmentalism in one line.”

A few are organised. The many aren’t.

£10 each ×50 million of us=£500 million →5 companies

“Are you going to give up a night at the pub to write to your MP over £10?”

Economics explains why we fail. It has few cures.

So how did we get from bands of dozens to eight billion?

“That’s a real mystery.”

Many names, one kind of challenge.

collective action problemtragedy of the commonsfree-rider problemsocial dilemmarace to the bottommultipolar trapMoloch

In this course: collective action. It can succeed as well as fail.

“If you like, it’s another word for cooperation. How do we cooperate?”

Our ability to act together: when it fails, when it succeeds, and how we make it succeed more.

“If you care about the planet, or even just you and your friends, you care about this.”

Collective action is the organ, not the cause.

“Different problems, different mixes.”

We’d all be better off acting together, and none of us can afford to go first alone.

Or worse: each of us does better breaking ranks, whatever the others do.

“The first is the playground. The second is the battle line, and the lobbyists.”

“It’s a multipolar trap.” “It’s Moloch.” True, but that only names the organ.

“Like saying the patient died of heart failure, and stopping.”

What would it take to cooperate on a planetary scale?

Climate.

The AI race, and powerful technology in general.

“To answer that, we’ll often have to go below collective action itself.”

Two misapprehensions

Two common misapprehensions, and they’re opposites.

1“It’s modernity’s fault.”

2“It’s an ascent of civilisation.”

“I want to address them up front.”

“Get rid of modernity, and we’d all cooperate.”

Some truth in it. Overall, a misapprehension.

“Our institutions can make things much worse. But look at animals.”
Clipabout 90 seconds

When the lions come: stand together, or run?

Play on YouTube Battle at Kruger, 2004 · Budzinski and Schlosberg
Play 60–90 s, from the herd turning back to the calf rejoining. After the clip: “Each buffalo, alone, is safer running. This time they come back together.” (Link is a YouTube search: the brief gives no URL for the original upload.)

Animals and every human society face it. Many find skilful answers.

We’re also wired to cooperate.

“That’s why the failures hurt.”

“History is progress. Thank God for civilisation.”

Some truth in it. Overall, a misapprehension.

“The scale of cooperation grew. Wellbeing often didn’t.”

Agriculture may have been the first great collective action trap.

Gatherer-hunters: healthier · more free time · more equal

But nobody could stay out alone.

“The evidence is mixed, but it’s a strong case.”

Cooperation comes in two forms.

Bottom-up

democratic

egalitarian

chosen

Coerced

the army

the Leviathan

fear of punishment

“Much of the growth in cooperation was driven by violence and oppression.”

The wisdom gap

We have the tools of gods with the minds of chimpanzees.

After E. O. Wilson

“I’m not saying bigger is better. We’re stuck with scale.”
